title: 30-Year Treasury Bond auction — the November refunding NEW issue, 1:00pm ET, the first bond session after the Veterans Day closure
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), re-fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-08 (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes) and its text layer decompressed stream-by-stream by THIS session, independently of the proposal that discovered it. Row reads verbatim `30-Year BOND / Wednesday, November 04, 2026 / Thursday, November 12, 2026 / Monday, November 16, 2026` — no trailing `R`, so a NEW ISSUE, announced by the 2026-11-04 quarterly refunding statement. The same PDF carries its own line `Holiday - Wednesday, November 11, 2026 - Veterans Day`, a Treasury primary for the closure this event sits behind. Settlement is Monday 11-16 because the customary 15th is a Sunday; the bond will be dated 2026-11-15 and back-dated, as every refunding 30-Year is. 1:00pm ET is Treasury's standing coupon-auction convention and is NOT separately sourced. Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-09-08 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, which read `proposals/treasury-30y-bond-2026-11-12.from-treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-11-12.json` in full first (EVENT-RESEARCH.md). TWO CORRECTIONS TO THAT PROPOSAL, both primary-derived. (1) The proposal's framing that 'a closed day sits inside a block that ran three consecutive business days in every other 2026 cycle' is true of CALENDAR days and misleading about SESSIONS: the bond market is shut on 11-11, so the 3Y (Mon 11-09), 10Y (Tue 11-10) and 30Y (Thu 11-12) still run on three CONSECUTIVE BOND SESSIONS, exactly as a normal Tue/Wed/Thu block does. Nothing is compressed, stretched, or displaced. (2) The shape is not novel. Measured this session from `auctions_query` across 2009-2025: whenever Veterans Day falls on a WEDNESDAY, Treasury runs Mon 3Y / Tue 10Y / [Wed closed] / Thu 30Y — 3 for 3 (2009-11-12, 2015-11-12, 2020-11-12), and 2026 is the fourth instance. Whenever it falls on a TUESDAY the closure sits between the 3Y and the 10Y instead (2014, 2025, 2 for 2). Across all 6 holiday-inside Novembers the 30Y anchored on THURSDAY, 6/6. EXPECTED SIZE, per the grid rather than any current document: $25B — 11 consecutive nominal 30-Year new issues at $25B since 2024-02-08, and no nominal coupon or FRN size has moved anywhere since April 2024. That number is not published today (sb0590's anticipated-size table ends at Oct-26) and becomes published on 2026-11-04. HEADLINE SUPPLY UNDERSTATES THE LINE: 15/15 nominal 30-Year new issues since 2023-02 took a positive SOMA add-on, averaging $5.75B on the $25B era (median $6.08B), so total accepted has run ~1.24x the offering. NO BUYBACK QUESTION HERE, unlike the 09-10 and 10-08 siblings: the published Tentative Buyback Schedule (re-fetched 2026-09-08, HTTP 200, byte-identical at 125,547 bytes to the 09-03 and 09-05 pulls, still mastheaded 'For Publication August 5, 2026' — sb0607's promised update is 20 days unfulfilled) ends at the 11/05/2026 operation. The week of this auction has no published operation calendar; the 11-04 refunding publishes it. The new bond will also be buyback-INELIGIBLE until after its first coupon on 2027-05-15, per the TreasuryDirect eligibility clauses the 10-08 sibling established 20/20. Read it, do not trade it: `symbols: []`, date is `estimate`, and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is rates-keyed.
